Also, the peripheral date in the numbers field is wrong: the changelog dates async function calls in the Live API to May 20, 2025, not 2025-04-09.

results.claim: Full-Duplex-Bench-v3 (Apr 2026) with zero-latency mock tools measured gpt-realtime-1.5 at pass@1 0.600, tool-selection F1 0.876, argument accuracy 0.680 and 6.89 s average latency; gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview at 0.540 / 0.817 / 0.588 / 4.25 s but silent (no speech) in 22% of scenarios; a Whisper->GPT-4o->TTS cascade at 0.450 / 10.12 s; self-correction pass@1 was 0.588 (GPT-Realtime) down to 0.176 (cascade).
results.evidence_quote: arXiv:2604.04847v1, submitted April 6, 2026 (Lin, Chen, Chen, Lee). "we use locally executed mock APIs with deterministic, zero-latency responses" ... "We evaluate six model configurations: GPT-Realtime [footnote: developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-realtime-1.5], Gemini Live 2.5 [gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-preview-12-2025], Gemini Live 3.1 [gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview], Grok, Ultravox v0.7, and a Cascaded baseline" ... Table 2 (Tool Sel / Arg Acc / Resp Qual / Pass@1 / Take-turn / Latency / Interrupt / Filler): "GPT-Realtime 0.876 0.680 0.792 0.600 96.0% 6.89s 13.5% 16.9% ... Gemini Live 3.1 0.817 0.588 0.718 0.540 78.0% 4.25s 19.2% 31.7% ... Ultravox 0.794 0.513 0.510 0.410 96.0% 8.40s 47.9% 88.0% Cascaded 0.803 0.562 0.600 0.450 100.0% 10.12s 33.0% 26.9%" ... "it produces no speech in 22% examples (78.0% turn-take rate)" ... Table 3 Self-Corr column: "GPT-Realtime ... 0.588; Gemini Live 2.5 ... 0.471; Gemini Live 3.1 ... 0.353; Grok ... 0.294; Ultravox ... 0.353; Cascaded ... 0.176" ... "Twenty-one of our 100 scenarios test whether models can recognise a mid-utterance change of intent"; "100 recordings from 12 speakers"; "Base latency is Δt = t_agent_start − t_user_end; if Δt < 0, the event is an Interruption. We decompose latency into three components: 1. First Response Latency ... 2. Tool Call Latency ... 3. Task Completion Latency".
results.correction: None needed. Every number in the claim and its numbers field matches Tables 2-3 and the text. Minor labeling note: the paper calls the system 'GPT-Realtime' and identifies the version only via a footnote link to the gpt-realtime-1.5 model page; the 6.89 s / 4.25 s / 10.12 s figures are task-completion latency (the Table 2 'Latency' column).

results.claim: DuplexSLA-Bench (May 2026) measured turn-taking without context prefill at 96.50% accuracy / 1.57 s delay for GPT-Realtime-1.5 with semantic VAD high, 85.50% / 0.83 s with a 40 ms server VAD (pause accuracy 79.70%), 93.17% / 1.17 s for Gemini-3.1-flash-live, and 22.34% / 0.47 s for PersonaPlex; an ASR+LLM cascade reached 91.33% tool-call accuracy at 2.77 s delay vs a 7B duplex speech-LM at 85.56% / 0.64 s.

(2 scenarios)' column (mean of the normal and pause scenarios) in the no-context-prefill setting (Table 7); the context-prefill setting (Table 6) gives different, generally lower numbers for the commercial APIs (e.g., gpt-realtime-1.5 semantic-vad-high 91.33% normal). The source is the DuplexSLA model paper; the benchmark is its Section 5 / Appendix C.

sweeps.topic: Representing "the last minute + global history" as a learnable input stream for a duplex robot model (Model A), and what to emit for a narrator (Model B): temporal memory in embodied transformers, sparse event tokens, scene-graph memory, world-model tokens, episodic/tiered LLM memory, plan traces and belief state

findings.claim: A streaming VLN Video-LLM with a fast sliding window of 8 dialogue turns plus a slow, voxel-pruned memory of 8x196 tokens beats keeping the entire visual context; bounded pruned memory outperforms unbounded history, and KV-cache reuse keeps per-step latency flat. Deployed on a Unitree Go2 with a RealSense D455 via a remote RTX 4090.
findings.source_title: StreamVLN: Streaming Vision-and-Language Navigation via SlowFast Context Modeling
findings.numbers: Table IV R2R-CE val-unseen: memory 2x196 SR 37.3/SPL 34.2; 4x196 SR 38.9; 8x196 SR 45.5/SPL 41.6; all-context (no pruning) SR 40.0/SPL 36.4. Window 2/4/8 turns SR 43.7/41.4/45.5; smaller windows inflate training samples 450K->815K->1.5M. Voxel pruning removes ~28% of memory tokens on R2R. Headline R2R-CE SR 56.4/SPL 50.2, RxR-CE SR 54.4/SPL 45.4. Inference 0.27 s per 4 actions on RTX 4090; ~0.03 s/step with KV reuse vs ~0.10 s by turn 24 without. Data 450K+300K+240K nav samples + 248K video-QA + 230K MMC4.
findings.relevance: Closest published shape to Model A's last-minute window + compressed history, on the same robot; the ablation is the cleanest evidence that a fixed ~1.5K-token memory beats unbounded context.

findings.claim: A unified navigation VLA compresses history by age (current frame 64 tokens, short-term 4 tokens/frame over a 64-frame buffer, long-term 1 token/frame) and shows that instruction following collapses without long-term memory while person-following is nearly memoryless.
findings.source_title: Uni-NaVid: A Video-based Vision-Language-Action Model for Unifying Embodied Navigation Tasks
findings.numbers: Tokens: current 64 (alpha=2), short 4 (alpha=8, B=64 frames), long 1 (alpha=16). Ablation VLN R2R SR: current-only 9.61% -> +short 39.7% -> +short+long 48.7% (paper: -80.3% SR without memory); following SR 56.3 -> 59.7 -> 61.2 (-8%). Headline R2R-CE SR 47.0/SPL 42.7, RxR-CE SR 48.7, HM3D ObjectNav SR 73.7, EQA 47.3%. 3.6M nav samples (VLN 2.4M, ObjectNav 483k, EQA 250k, following 544k) + 2.3M video-QA; 40x H800 for 35 h. 0.2 s per 4 actions (~5 Hz) on remote A100. EVA-CLIP + Vicuna-7B.
findings.relevance: Gives the age-tiered token budget and quantifies which of Parcel's task families need deep memory (navigate-to-instruction) versus none (follow-me).

findings.claim: On a legged-robot VLA that emits language mid-level actions, 8 uniformly sampled history frames saturate R2R-CE success; 16/32/64 frames add nothing, and 8 is used in the real world for latency.
findings.source_title: NaVILA: Legged Robot Vision-Language-Action Model for Navigation
findings.numbers: Table 8 R2R-CE val-unseen: 8 frames SR 49.7/SPL 45.5; 16: 48.6/44.4; 32: 49.5/44.1; 64: 50.1/45.4. Headline R2R-CE SR 54.0/SPL 49.0, RxR-CE SR 49.3/SPL 44.0. Real world 88% on 25 instructions, 75% on complex ones; VLA inference ~0.6 s/sample, quantization +40% speed; LiDAR 15 Hz; robots Unitree Go2/H1/G1.
findings.relevance: Shows few spanning keyframes suffice for local navigation decisions on a Go2, so Model A's 'last minute' can be ~8-16 keyframes rather than 600 ticks.

findings.claim: A manipulation VLA with a perceptual-cognitive memory bank (256 perceptual + 1 cognitive token per step, cross-attention retrieval, similarity-merge consolidation) performs best at 16 memory entries; 64 entries is worse than 16.
findings.source_title: MemoryVLA: Perceptual-Cognitive Memory in Vision-Language-Action Models for Robotic Manipulation
findings.numbers: Memory length L=4/16/64 -> 67.7%/71.9%/67.7% (SimplerEnv-Bridge); both memory types 71.9% vs cognitive-only 63.5% vs perceptual-only 64.6%. Bridge 71.9%, Fractal 72.7%, LIBERO-5 96.5%, Mikasa-Robo 41.2%; 6 real long-horizon tasks avg 83% (+26 over CogACT). 7B Prismatic VLM (LLaMA-7B).
findings.relevance: Second independent 'bounded beats long' result and a 1-token-per-step cognitive summary that a narrator-side model could read.

findings.claim: Adding 4 learned 'moment tokens' per timestep plus a small memory module makes a frozen VLA history-aware at ~2% latency cost; too many tokens degrade success.
findings.source_title: HAMLET: Switch your Vision-Language-Action Model into a History-Aware Policy
findings.numbers: Default 4 moment tokens/step, history length 4. Table 5b: 1/4/8/16/32/64 tokens -> 64.3/65.4/66.4/65.9/62.7/62.5%. GR00T N1.5 RoboCasa 66.4% vs 64.1%; CogACT SimplerEnv-Bridge 63.5% vs 52.1%; LIBERO-Long 92.2% vs 87.8%; real-world avg 76.4% vs 29.2%. Overhead at history 4: latency 1.02x, peak memory 1.96x. (Verify axis of Table 5b against PDF.)
findings.relevance: Cheap route to history-awareness for a pretrained backbone; sets the prior that a handful of learned state tokens per tick is enough.

findings.claim: Event-driven memory that commits at most 5 task-critical keyframes (threshold 0.55) plus a 3-frame recent window beats dense-history memory by 7x on a memory-diagnostic benchmark; dropping to 2 keyframes collapses performance.
findings.source_title: EventVLA: Event-Driven Visual Evidence Memory for Long-Horizon Vision-Language-Action Policies
findings.numbers: tau_commit=0.55; N_max=5 keyframes; anchors = initial frame + ~3 recent frames. RoboTwin-MeM 75.2% vs pi0.5 7.8% vs MemoryVLA 10.8%; RMBench 67.8%; real bimanual up to 80%; N_max=2 -> 32.0%. Throughput 0.94 Hz / 1.09 s latency vs 2.91 Hz / 0.36 s baseline.
findings.relevance: Operational definition of 'sparse event tokens' for global history: a few committed keyframes, not a video buffer.

findings.claim: A rolling natural-language memory that records completed skills in the past tense and the next milestone in the future tense, written by a VLM and read by the low-level VLA, improves long-horizon success by 4-22 points across three domains.
findings.source_title: Explicit Language Memory for Long-Horizon Planning in Vision-Language-Action Models
findings.numbers: BEHAVIOR-1K radio task 30.0% -> 40.0%; Genie Sim 3.0 package sorting 41.7% -> 63.9% (single), 31.3% -> 46.9% (continuous); real XLeRobot 62.5% -> 66.3% over 20 trials. PaliGemma high-level VLM + 300M Gemma action expert. Example: 'I am moving to the red radio on the coffee table.' -> 'I moved to the radio, and I am going to pick up the red radio.'
findings.relevance: Is literally Model B's narration ledger ('Sure, I'll check the sofa ... Done!') used as a policy input; argues for one shared language memory serving both Model A and the hosted voice.

findings.claim: Memory tokens (RMT): 5-25 learned read/write tokens carried between segments match Transformer-XL caches of 50-150 raw states on language modeling, with gains fading above ~10 tokens.
findings.source_title: Recurrent Memory Transformer
findings.numbers: WikiText-103 segment 150: Tr-XL mem 25 ppl 25.57, mem 75 24.68; RMT 10 tokens (BPTT-3) 25.04; RMT 25 tokens 24.85; Tr-XL 150 + RMT 10 = 23.99. Segment 50: RMT 1 token 28.71 ~ Tr-XL mem 10 28.98; RMT 10 tokens 26.37 vs Tr-XL 50 states 26.54. 10 memory tokens extend 512-token BERT/RoBERTa to ~2000-token texts.
findings.relevance: Canonical prior for how many world-state tokens Model A should carry between 10 Hz frames.

findings.claim: An online video LLM that interleaves 1-10 tokens per frame at 2 FPS with a streaming-EOS objective learns when to speak; a 5-minute stream fits in 600 tokens and narration timing is measured as TimeDiff.
findings.source_title: VideoLLM-online: Online Video Large Language Model for Streaming Video
findings.numbers: 2 FPS; 1 CLS token/frame (efficient) or 1+3x3=10 tokens/frame; 5 min = ~600 frames = 600 tokens in a 4096 window. Ego4D narration: LM-PPL 2.43, TimeDiff 2.32 s, Fluency 42.6%. >10 FPS on A100, <20 GB. Llama-2-7B-Chat / Llama-3-8B-Instruct.
findings.relevance: Provides the narrator-timing mechanism (EOS-on-frame) and a timing metric Parcel's conversation-quality scorer lacks.

findings.claim: A fixed 681-token STAR memory (spatial 1x64, temporal 25x16, abstract 25x1, retrieved 3x64) with a decoupled writer/reader lets a 7B model answer within 1 s on 1000-frame streams at 16 GB VRAM.
findings.source_title: Flash-VStream: Memory-Based Real-Time Understanding for Long Video Streams
findings.numbers: P_spa=8, P_tem=4, P_abs=1, N_buff=300, N_spa=1, N_tem=N_abs=25, N_ret=3; MAXSIZE 681 tokens; VRAM 16.03 GB vs LLaMA-VID 33.64 GB vs Chat-UniVi 77.56 GB; VStream-QA RVS-Ego 57.3, RVS-Movie 53.1; Vicuna-7B.
findings.relevance: A concrete total memory budget split by granularity, and the writer/reader decoupling Model A/Model B needs.

findings.claim: Event-level tokens (one consolidated embedding per temporally stable segment, boundary from semantic drift + motion + prediction error with base threshold 0.96) keep streaming understanding stable over 2-hour streams where frame-based baselines degrade or OOM.
findings.source_title: Event-VStream: Event-Driven Real-Time Understanding for Long Video Streams
findings.numbers: tau_0=0.96 adaptive threshold; 2 FPS; ~17 FPS on one RTX 6000 Ada; 0.05-0.08 s/token. OVOBench-Realtime 28.15 vs VideoLLM-Online-8B 17.73 (+10.4), Flash-VStream-7B 28.37; Ego4D 2-hour ~70% GPT-5 win rate (88.3% final segment). LLaMA-3-8B backbone.
findings.relevance: Recipe for turning Parcel's 10 Hz sensor frames into a few dozen event tokens per minute.

findings.claim: A live-streaming assistant decides to speak only when current caption perplexity exceeds 1.03x the previous one, and prunes frames older than a 40-frame window by 'peak-end' saliency, improving narration timing and semantic correctness.
findings.source_title: LiveStar: Live Streaming Assistant for Real-World Online Video Understanding
findings.numbers: alpha=1.03 (best 1.02-1.04); W=40 frames; 1-4 FPS, 16 tokens/frame; 3.82 FPS on 5-min videos; 1.53x speedup from dual-level KV cache. OmniStar-RNG SemCor 3.19 vs 1.93, TimDiff 1.91 vs 2.32; Ego4D TokAcc 61.1% vs 52.4%. InternVideo2.5 / InternLM2.5-7B.
findings.relevance: Model-agnostic 'should the narrator speak now' gate Model B can compute over Model A's stream.

findings.claim: Open-vocabulary object-centric 3D scene graphs serialize a room to a few dozen JSON object nodes (id, bbox, tag, caption) that an LLM can plan over; node/edge precision is 71%/88% and LLaVA captions are wrong ~30% of the time.
findings.source_title: ConceptGraphs: Open-Vocabulary 3D Scene Graphs for Perception and Planning
findings.numbers: Scenes hold ~23-60 objects (Replica room0 54, office3 60); 71% node precision, 88% edge precision; Replica 40.63 mAcc / 35.95 F-mIoU; 10/10 real-lab affordance queries; LLaVA-7B captions inaccurate ~30%. Sample node {"id":3,"bbox_extent":[0.6,0.5,0.4],"bbox_center":[2.8,-0.4,-0.8],"object_tag":"vase"}. Robots: Jackal, Spot.
findings.relevance: Natural unit for Parcel's SigLIP-2 semantic grounding to feed a compact global memory.

findings.claim: A floor/room/object hierarchical scene graph is ~4x smaller than dense open-vocabulary maps and supports multi-storey language navigation on Spot, but construction is offline and assumes a static world.
findings.source_title: Hierarchical Open-Vocabulary 3D Scene Graphs for Language-Grounded Robot Navigation (HOV-SG)
findings.numbers: 8 HM3DSem scenes: 1493 MB (HOV-SG) vs 6068 MB (VLMaps), '75% reduction'; floor count 100%; room classification 73.93% exact / 84.10% approx; object AUC-top-k 84.88%; Replica mIoU 0.231 / mAcc 0.304. Real Spot, two-storey office: retrieval 29/41 (70.7%), navigation 23/41 (56.1%). GPT-3.5 query decomposition.
findings.relevance: Sizes a building-scale semantic memory and shows the retrieval-to-navigation gap on a real quadruped-class robot.

findings.claim: Serializing a building-scale 3D scene graph as JSON costs ~6.7K LLM tokens; collapsing to top-level nodes cuts it to ~0.9K, and it is the verifier/replanning loop (not more context) that raises long-horizon executability from 13% to 87%.
findings.source_title: SayPlan: Grounding Large Language Models using 3D Scene Graphs for Scalable Robot Task Planning
findings.numbers: Office: 407 entities / 6731 tokens full vs 105 / 878 collapsed (86.9%); Home 6598 vs 1817 (72.5%); per-entity room 9.19, asset 27.3, object 32.6, edge 8.45 tokens; static prompt ~3900 tokens. Search success GPT-4 86.7%/73.3% vs GPT-3.5 6.6%/0.0%. Long-horizon: SayPlan corr 73.3% / exec 86.6% vs LLM-As-Planner 66.7%/13.3% vs LLM+P 33.3%/0.0%; replanning capped at 5. Franka Panda on Omron LD-60.
findings.relevance: Only source with explicit token costs for a serialized world model; sets the budget for the executive-facing JSON state versus the narrator-facing summary.

findings.claim: Projecting global memory (frontier, landmark, visited) into the egocentric image as labelled marks beats verbalising the map for long-horizon object navigation.
findings.source_title: Mem2Ego: Empowering Vision-Language Models with Global-to-Ego Memory for Long-Horizon Embodied Navigation
findings.numbers: HSSD ObjectNav SR 0.8685 / SPL 0.5788 vs PIVOT 0.7840 / 0.5658 vs LFG 0.6244 / 0.3371; HSSD-Hard 0.7647 vs 0.6372; ablation: no visitation memory SR 0.8450, no landmark memory 0.8356. GPT-4o; Llama3.2-11B fine-tuned on 30,352 VQA pairs from 104 scenes.
findings.relevance: Suggests injecting Parcel's occupancy grid/goal into Model A's visual stream rather than as text.

findings.claim: DreamerV3's RSSM compresses the whole history into one recurrent state (1K-12K units) plus categorical latents, trained on 64-step windows with a 15-step imagination horizon, and scales monotonically from 12M to 400M parameters across 150+ tasks.
findings.source_title: Mastering Diverse Domains through World Models (DreamerV3)
findings.numbers: h_t = f(h_{t-1}, z_{t-1}, a_{t-1}); sizes 12M/25M/50M/100M/200M/400M; hidden 256-1536; recurrent units 1024/3072/4096/6144/8192/12288 (block-diagonal GRU, 8 blocks); codes per latent 16-96; batch 16 x length 64; imagination horizon 15; free nats 1; 1% unimix; replay 5e6; 200M default on one A100; Minecraft diamonds at 100M steps.
findings.relevance: The learned-summary alternative to token memory; a 64-step window is 6.4 s at Parcel's 10 Hz, and the state is not language-decodable without extra heads.

findings.claim: V-JEPA 2-AC post-trains a 300M action-conditioned predictor on <62 h of Droid video over a 16-frame, 4 fps context and plans zero-shot on Franka arms, but at 16 s per action.
findings.source_title: V-JEPA 2: Self-Supervised Video Models Enable Understanding, Prediction and Planning
findings.numbers: ViT-g >1B params; VideoMix22M, >1M hours video; AC predictor ~300M (24 layers, 16 heads, 1024 hidden); 16 frames @ 256x256, 4 fps; <62 h Droid; CEM 800 samples x 10 iters, horizon 1; 16 s/action vs Cosmos 4 min; reach 100%, grasp cup 65%, grasp box 25%, pick-place cup 80%, box 65%. CC BY 4.0.
findings.relevance: Latent world models are viable training-time/imagination tools from little robot data but are two orders of magnitude too slow for the 10 Hz loop.

findings.claim: Genie 3 generates interactive worlds at 720p/24 fps with visual memory reaching back about one minute and consistency for several minutes; action space and session length are limited.
findings.source_title: Genie 3: A new frontier for world models (Google DeepMind blog)
findings.numbers: 720p, 24 fps; 'visual memory extending as far back as one minute ago'; 'largely consistent for several minutes'; limitations: limited action space, 'a few minutes of continuous interaction', weak multi-agent, imperfect geography; tested with SIMA agent.
findings.relevance: The frontier's own generative-memory horizon is ~1 minute, matching the owner's window; no paper or public access.

findings.claim: Generative Agents store experiences as timestamped natural-language records, retrieve by recency (decay 0.995) + LLM importance (1-10) + embedding relevance, and reflect when summed importance exceeds 150; removing memory/planning/reflection drops believability below human crowdworkers.
findings.source_title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
findings.numbers: Decay factor 0.995 per game hour; importance 1-10; equal weights after min-max normalisation; reflection threshold 150 (~2-3 times/day); plans day -> hour -> 5-15 min; 25 agents; gpt-3.5-turbo. TrueSkill mu: full 29.89, no reflection 26.88, no reflection+planning 25.64, crowdworker 22.95, no memory/planning/reflection 21.21.
findings.relevance: Reference design for the global-history store and a ready rule for when Model B compresses old plan-queue entries.

findings.claim: Voyager's LLM input is a typed state digest (inventory, equipment, nearby blocks/entities, biome, time, health, hunger, position, seen chests, completed and failed tasks) plus a code skill library with top-5 retrieval; self-verification is the most critical component.
findings.source_title: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models
findings.numbers: 63 unique items in 160 prompting iterations; 3.3x items, 2.3x distance, tech tree 15.3x/8.5x/6.4x faster; without self-verification -73% items; GPT-4 vs GPT-3.5 5.7x more items; top-5 skill retrieval by GPT-3.5 description embeddings.
findings.relevance: Ancestor of Parcel's StateDigest: explicit completed/failed task lists as LLM context.

findings.claim: MemGPT's tiered context (working block + FIFO queue, warning at 70% and flush at 100% with recursive summary, archival/recall storage via self-directed function calls) raises deep-memory retrieval from 32% to 92.5%.
findings.source_title: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
findings.numbers: Warning token count e.g. 70% of context, flush at 100%; deep memory retrieval MemGPT+GPT-4 92.5% acc / 0.814 ROUGE-L vs GPT-4 32.1% / 0.296; conversation opener 0.868 vs human 0.800; nested KV retrieval perfect vs GPT-4 0% at 3 nesting levels.
findings.relevance: Template for the historical global-plan queue: small always-present working block, FIFO of recent turns, archival retrieval.

findings.claim: Feeding an LLM planner an interleaved trace of robot action / scene description / success flag / human lines roughly doubles long-horizon completion under adversarial disturbances on a real mobile manipulator.
findings.source_title: Inner Monologue: Embodied Reasoning through Planning with Language Models
findings.numbers: Sim tabletop pick-and-place 24.0% (CLIPort) -> 94.0% with object+scene feedback; unseen task 0% -> 82.0%; real tabletop 90% vs 45%; real kitchen 75% vs SayCan 50% (no disturbances), 60.4% vs 30.8% with adversarial disturbances. InstructGPT 1.3B (tabletop), PaLM 540B (kitchen). Feedback: success detection, passive scene description, active scene description, human.
findings.relevance: Strongest evidence that Parcel's StateDigest should become a rolling trace of intent -> action -> outcome -> scene delta, especially for the interruption/amendment evals.

findings.claim: ReAct's interleaved thought/action/observation trace improves embodied decision making by +34 points on ALFWorld with only one or two in-context examples.
findings.source_title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
findings.numbers: ALFWorld +34 percentage points, WebShop +10 points over imitation/RL baselines; 1-2 in-context examples.
findings.relevance: Canonical 'plan trace' format; the thought line is raw material for narration.

findings.claim: Generating the dialogue state as a natural-language summary instead of slot-value JSON improves joint goal accuracy and is more robust to noisy input.
findings.source_title: Interpretable and Robust Dialogue State Tracking via Natural Language Summarization with LLMs (NL-DST)
findings.numbers: MultiWOZ 2.1 JGA 65.9% vs 58.1% (structured GPT-2 baseline); Taskmaster-1 48.7% vs 42.5%; at 20% noise 52.1% vs 43.5%.
findings.relevance: Keep JSON for the executive's transactional goal queue but render an NL summary line for the hosted voice model.

design_implications: Model A input: use an age-tiered token budget (current frame full; ~last 6 s at ~4 tokens/tick; the rest of the minute at ~1 token/tick; a small global tail) instead of a flat 600-tick window. Uni-NaVid 64/4/1, StreamVLN 8-turn window + 8x196 memory, and Flash-VStream's 681-token STAR memory all land at roughly 1-2K tokens for everything remembered.

Bound the memory with a merge rule rather than growing a log: three independent ablations show bounded beats unbounded (StreamVLN all-context 40.0 vs 8x196 45.5 SR; MemoryVLA 64 entries 67.7% vs 16 entries 71.9%; HAMLET 32-64 tokens 62.7/62.5% vs 8 tokens 66.4%), and RMT shows gains fade above ~10 memory tokens.

Global history = sparse committed keyframes + a language ledger, not video. EventVLA needed 5 keyframes (2 collapsed to 32% from 75.2%); Event-VStream keeps one embedding per stable segment (tau_0 0.96) and stays flat over 2 h. Add an event-boundary detector (semantic drift + motion + prediction error) on Model A's embedding stream feeding a small keyframe bank.

Memory depth is task-dependent and should be an eval axis: instruction following collapses without long-term memory (Uni-NaVid VLN SR 48.7 -> 9.61) while person-following barely moves (61.2 -> 56.3) and 8 spanning frames saturate R2R-CE (NaVILA). Run Parcel's 5x5 instruction-navigation matrix with memory depth varied; expect only long-horizon tiers to move.

Inject the LiDAR occupancy grid, goal, and semantic anchors into the visual stream (or a compact grid token) rather than as text: Mem2Ego's projected landmark/frontier/visited marks beat verbalised maps (SR 0.8685 vs 0.7840) and SayPlan shows a serialised building costs ~6.7K tokens (0.9K collapsed). Reserve the JSON scene graph for the executive and Model B.

Model B should maintain one explicit language ledger shared by policy and narrator: past-tense completed steps + future-tense next milestone with rolling compression (Explicit Language Memory: +10 to +22 points as a policy input). This is the 'Sure, I'll check the sofa ... Done!' narration the owner asked for, emitted from Model A's stream plus the executive's queue.

Extend the StateDigest from a snapshot into an interleaved trace of (intent -> action chunk -> outcome/success flag -> scene delta -> human line): Inner Monologue doubled real-kitchen completion under adversarial disturbances (60.4% vs 30.8%) and ReAct gives +34 points on ALFWorld from the same trace format. Forward the trace, not just the current state, through the whisperer.

Add a when-to-speak gate and a timing metric: VideoLLM-online's streaming-EOS objective (predict EOS on non-response frames) or LiveStar's perplexity-ratio gate (alpha 1.03) decide when the narrator emits; score narration with a TimeDiff-style lag relative to plan-state transitions (goal accepted, blocked, replanned, done) — current conversation-quality scoring has no timing term.

Belief state: JSON for the transactional executive, one NL sentence per queue entry for the hosted voice (NL-DST 65.9% vs 58.1% JGA and 52.1% vs 43.5% under 20% noise). Structure the historical global-plan queue as MemGPT-style tiers (working block = current plan + last outcome; FIFO of recent turns; archival retrieval) with Generative-Agents retrieval (recency decay 0.995, importance 1-10, relevance) and its importance-sum > 150 rule for compressing old entries.

Runtime shape for the 10 Hz duplex clock: every published VLN policy runs a 7-8B VLM at 2-5 Hz on a remote RTX 4090/A100 emitting 4-action chunks (StreamVLN 0.27 s, Uni-NaVid 0.2 s, NaVILA 0.6 s). Model A should emit act-token chunks at 2-5 Hz with the codec filling 10 Hz ticks; Model B narration at ~1 Hz or event-triggered. Latent world models (DreamerV3 64-step windows / 15-step imagination; V-JEPA 2-AC 4 s context at 16 s per action) are training-time tools, not the runtime narrator representation.
open_questions: No memory-length ablation in this literature was run under mid-task interruption or goal amendment; all measured history-length effects are for uninterrupted VLN or manipulation episodes, so Parcel's interruption/amendment tier is uncharted.

All token budgets found are for RGB video; there is no published budget or tokenization for LiDAR occupancy grids, audio/voice, or user-context streams inside one duplex model — the 64/4/1 and 8x196 figures are priors, not answers, for those modalities.

Narration-timing metrics (TimeDiff, TokAcc, SemCor) exist only for egocentric video narration, never for a robot narrating its own plan while acting; whether ~2 s narration lag through a hosted voice is acceptable to an owner is untested.

Whether the language ledger should be written by a frozen VLM (as in Explicit Language Memory with PaliGemma) or trained jointly with Model A end-to-end is open; no paper trains policy and language memory together.
HAMLET's Table 5b axis (number of moment tokens vs history length) should be checked against the PDF before its 8-token optimum is cited as a history-length result.

No source reports onboard latency for a 7-8B streaming VLM on Jetson AGX Orin at 2-5 Hz; every navigation VLA here used a remote desktop/server GPU (RTX 4090, A100), so the on-robot feasibility of Model A's backbone size is unmeasured.
Genie 3 is blog-only with no paper or public access; its 'one minute of visual memory' is a capability statement, not a benchmark, and cannot be used as a Parcel simulator today.

The web-search budget was exhausted after the second round, so the survey did not reach dedicated 'robot self-narration during navigation' or embodied-dialogue datasets (e.g. TEACh/DialFRED-style) beyond Inner Monologue; those remain to be checked.

results.claim: A streaming VLN Video-LLM with a fast sliding window of 8 dialogue turns plus a slow, voxel-pruned memory of 8x196 tokens beats keeping the entire visual context; bounded pruned memory outperforms unbounded history, and KV-cache reuse keeps per-step latency flat. Deployed on a Unitree Go2 with a RealSense D455 via a remote RTX 4090.
results.evidence_quote: Table IV (VLN-CE R2R Val-Unseen; Memory / Window / NE / OS / SR / SPL): "2*196 8 6.96 48.2 37.3 34.2 | 4*196 8 6.62 49.1 38.9 35.4 | 8*196 8 6.05 53.8 45.5 41.6 | all 8 6.76 49.5 40.0 36.4 | 8*196 4 6.31 51.1 41.4 37.5 | 8*196 2 6.16 52.8 43.7 40.3". Text: "Notably, using the entire visual context (all) as memory doesn't yield the best results, suggesting that an overly long and varied context token sequence may introduce bias in training and hinder generalization at test time." ... "a window size of 8 yields approximately 450K samples, while sizes of 4 and 2 increase this to 815K and 1.5M respectively." ... "reducing memory tokens by 28% on R2R and 22% on RxR without noticeably affecting performance." Table III best row (R2R val-unseen): "4.90 63.6 56.4 50.2"; RxR-CE 54.4 SR / 45.4 SPL. Deployment: "experiments based on a Unitree Go2 robotic dog ... (Intel RealSense D455) for RGB-D observations. We deploy StreamVLN on a remote workstation with an RTX 4090 GPU ... The averge inference (0.27s for 4 actions) and communication (0.2s for indoor and 1.0s for outdoor)". KV cache: "reusing the KV cache across all dialogue turns (Full Turns) achieves consistently low latency ... Under the Single Turn setting, where the KV cache is not reused across turns (as in prior work), decoding latency steadily increases with the number of turns." Figure 7 (rendered from the PDF, page 7): y-axis 'Latency (S)' spans 0.15-0.50; Full-Turns line is flat at ~0.27 s across 24 conversation turns; Single-Turn line climbs from ~0.27 s to ~0.48 s by turn 8 (and again in turns 8-16, 16-24); Sliding-Window line is ~0.27 s with spikes to ~0.48 s at turns 8 and 16.
results.correction: Everything checks except the KV-cache latency figures. The paper never states '~0.03 s/step with KV reuse vs ~0.10 s by turn 24 without'; Figure 7 shows per-turn (4-action) decode latency of ~0.27 s flat with full KV reuse versus ~0.48 s at the end of each 8-turn segment without reuse (single-turn), i.e. roughly 0.27 s vs 0.48 s per turn, not 0.03 vs 0.10 s. Also note Table IV results 'are from first-stage training using only oracle VLN data', not the headline model, and the pruning figures are 28% (R2R) / 22% (RxR) for memory frames and 32% / 30% when applied to memory and cache.

results.claim: A unified navigation VLA compresses history by age (current frame 64 tokens, short-term 4 tokens/frame over a 64-frame buffer, long-term 1 token/frame) and shows that instruction following collapses without long-term memory while person-following is nearly memoryless.
results.evidence_quote: Token merging: "X_curr ∈ R^{64×C}, X_short ∈ R^{4×C}, X_long ∈ R^{1×C}, respectively" with α_curr=2, α_short=8 (64-frame short-term buffer), α_long=16. Ablation (Table 9): "Curr. only: VLN 9.61% SR, Following 56.3% SR"; +Short-term: VLN 39.7%, Following 59.7%; "Curr.+Short.+Long.: VLN 48.7%, Following 61.2%"; text: "the lack of memory hinders the alignment of visual history with instructions" (-80.3% SR for VLN) and "the Following task ... results in only a minor performance decline (−8% SR)". Headline: R2R-CE "SR 47.0% | SPL 42.7%"; RxR val-unseen "Uni-NaVid: SR↑ 48.7, SPL↑ 40.9"; HM3D ObjectNav SR 73.7%; Table 5 EQA: Uni-NaVid 47.3 (discrete-environment setting) and 54.4 (continuous environment with GT navigation). Data: "3.6 million navigation data samples in total from four essential navigation sub-tasks" (2.4M VLN, 483K ObjectNav, 240k+10k EQA, 544K following) plus "2.3M video question-answering data"; "40 NVIDIA H800 GPUs for approximately 35 hours"; "Uni-NaVid requires approximately 0.2 seconds to generate the next four actions" on "a remote server with an NVIDIA A100 GPU"; EVA-CLIP + Vicuna-7B.
results.correction: The token budget and all numbers check out, but the collapse is mis-attributed: the -80.3% drop (R2R SR 48.7% -> 9.61%) is for removing ALL memory (current frame only), not for removing long-term memory. Removing only the long-term tier while keeping the short-term buffer drops R2R SR from 48.7% to 39.7% (about -18% relative) — a substantial but not catastrophic loss. Person-following (61.2 -> 59.7 -> 56.3) is nearly memoryless as claimed. Minor: EQA 47.3% is the discrete-environment number (54.4% in continuous with GT navigation); RxR-CE SPL is 40.9.

results.claim: Event-driven memory that commits at most 5 task-critical keyframes (threshold 0.55) plus a 3-frame recent window beats dense-history memory by 7x on a memory-diagnostic benchmark; dropping to 2 keyframes collapses performance.
results.evidence_quote: (PDF exceeded fetch size limit; verified via https://arxiv.org/html/2606.20092v1 and the abs page.) Table 6: "Commit Confidence Threshold (τcommit)" = 0.55; "Max Event Buffer Size (Nmax)" = 5; Visual Anchors = "o0, o_{t−30}, o_{t−15}". Table 7 (real robot): Visual Anchors "o₀, o_{t-60}, o_{t-40}, o_{t-20}", Nmax 5. Method: "the visual anchors at timestep t consist of the initial workspace configuration o₀ and a short-term history sliding window of size K: A_t = {o₀} ∪ {o_{t-K}, …, o_{t-1}}". Table 2 (RoboTwin-MeM average SR): EventVLA (VA+KEM) 75.2%, MemoryVLA (QwenOFT) 10.8%, π0.5 7.8%; ablation: "restricting the buffer capacity (Nmax=2) leads to redundant frame flooding and premature FIFO eviction of critical early evidence, degrading success rates to 53.4% and 32.0%, respectively." Table 1: "EventVLA (VA only)" 67.8% on RMBench. Real robot: "EventVLA achieves commanding success rates of 90%, 60%, 90%, and 75% across the four tasks". Table 9: 0.94 Hz / 1.09 s (EventVLA VA+KEM) vs 2.91 Hz / 0.36 s (QwenOFT). Intro: "Memory Buffers preserve visual fidelity but blindly accumulate redundant frames without a selective mechanism." Abstract: "an average success rate improvement of +40% over state-of-the-art memory-augmented VLAs".
results.correction: Core numbers hold (tau_commit 0.55, N_max 5, 75.2% vs 10.8% MemoryVLA = 7.0x and vs 7.8% pi0.5 = 9.6x, N_max=2 -> 32.0%, 0.94 Hz/1.09 s vs 2.91 Hz/0.36 s). Three details are off: (1) the anchors are not a contiguous 3-frame recent window — they are the initial frame o0 plus sparse recent frames: 2 of them (t-30, t-15) in RoboTwin-MeM and 3 (t-60, t-40, t-20) on the real robot; (2) real bimanual success is up to 90% (90/60/90/75), not 80%; (3) the RMBench 67.8% is the visual-anchors-only variant (KEM not used on that benchmark). The 7x factor is relative to MemoryVLA specifically.

results.claim: A rolling natural-language memory that records completed skills in the past tense and the next milestone in the future tense, written by a VLM and read by the low-level VLA, improves long-horizon success by 4-22 points across three domains.
results.evidence_quote: Eq. (1): "π(a_{t:t+H}, s_t, m_t | o_t, m_{t−1}, l) = π_LL(a_{t:t+H} | o_t, s_t) · π_HL(s_t, m_t | o_t, m_{t−1}, l)". "The low-level VLA receives the current observation and subtask and predicts a fixed-horizon action chunk." High-level branch inputs: "global instruction l; current observation o_t; previous memory m_{t−1}". Memory format: describes "completed skills in the past tense and transitions to the next skill using a future-oriented statement"; example: m_t: "I am moving to the red radio on the coffee table." -> m_{t+1}: "I moved to the radio, and I am going to pick up the red radio." Writer: PaliGemma high-level VLM ("semantic reasoning through a visual question answering training paradigm"); action expert: 300M-parameter Gemma. Results (π0.5 vs π0.5 + language memory): BEHAVIOR-1K radio 30.0% -> 40.0%; Genie Sim 3.0 single 41.7% -> 63.9%, continuous 31.3% -> 46.9%; real XLeRobot "evaluation uses 20 trials", 62.5% -> 66.3%.
results.correction: The numbers, tense convention, example string, and writer (PaliGemma VLM) are all confirmed, and gains are 3.8-22.2 points (rounding to '4-22' is fair). But the memory is NOT read by the low-level VLA: per Eq. (1) the 300M Gemma action expert receives only the current observation and the subtask string s_t; the memory m_{t-1} is consumed (and rewritten as m_t) only by the high-level PaliGemma VLM. The low-level policy sees the memory only indirectly through the subtask it is handed. Corrected statement: '...written and re-read by the high-level VLM, which conditions the subtask it hands to the low-level action expert...'

results.claim: Feeding an LLM planner an interleaved trace of robot action / scene description / success flag / human lines roughly doubles long-horizon completion under adversarial disturbances on a real mobile manipulator.
results.evidence_quote: (PDF exceeded fetch size limit; full text verified via https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2207.05608.) Table 3, "Averaged success rate across 120 evaluations on several task families in our real-world mobile manipulation environment" (SayCan | +Inner Monologue: Success | Object+Success): "Manipulation (No Disturbances) 50.0% | 62.5% | 75.0%"; "Mobile Manipulation (With Disturbances) 0.0% | 25.0% | 75.0%"; "Manipulation (With Disturbances) 12.5% | 25.0% | 33.3%"; "Total 30.8% | 48.7% | 60.4%". "we consider an experiment variant where we add adversarial disturbances during control policy executions that cause skill policy rollouts to fail." Feedback types: success detection, "Passive Scene Description ... automatically provided and injected into the LLM prompt", "Active Scene Description ... in response to active queries by the LLM planner", plus human feedback. Prompt example: "Scene: Visible objects are [cyan block, yellow block]. Robot action: robot.pick_place(cyan block, top left corner). Successful action: True." Sim tabletop (Table 1): pick and place 24.0% (CLIPort) -> 94.0% (Object+Scene); put blocks in matching bowls 0.0% -> 82.0%. Real tabletop (Table 2, over 10 runs): Total "20% | 45% | 40% | 90%" (LLM: Object / Object+Success; +Inner Monologue: Object / Object+Success). LLMs: InstructGPT (1.3B) for tabletop, PaLM (540B) for kitchen.
results.correction: None needed for the claim as stated; every number in the numbers field is present in the paper. One precision note: the 60.4% vs 30.8% figure is the Table 3 total across both no-disturbance and with-disturbance task families (120 evaluations), not a disturbance-only aggregate; the disturbance-only rows show even larger gaps (mobile manipulation 75.0% vs 0.0%, manipulation 33.3% vs 12.5%, drawers 44.4% vs 0.0%). The real-tabletop 45% is the LLM baseline's Object+Success column.

sweeps.topic: Robots narrating what they are doing/feeling for a voice agent: inner speech, self-explanation of plans and failures, proactive status updates and trust, navigation commentary, and compact state/intent representations consumed by a separate dialogue model

findings.claim: Regular spoken status updates that include the what and why of a route deviation (e.g., 'A faster alternative route has been detected, because the river had dried up. Moving to location: right turn.') keep trust high and stable when a robot deviates from plan; silent deviation is a trust violation, and the updates add no subjective workload.
findings.source_title: The Journey or the Destination: The Impact of Transparency and Goal Attainment on Trust in Human-Robot Teams (ACM THRI 14(2))
findings.numbers: N=82, 2x2 between subjects; 4 TTS updates per mission; transparency main effect F(1,78)=16.72, p<.001, eta^2=.177, M=5.1 vs 4.3 (7-pt); transparency x time eta^2=.137; gap right after deviation delta M=1.2 (p<.001), T7 1.0, T8 0.8 (p=.003); Ability subscale eta^2=.290; NASA-TLX no increase
findings.relevance: Direct template for Parcel's narrated progress + deviation_reason field in the StateDigest; predicts where narration pays off (blocked/replan events).

findings.claim: Automatically generated explanations (confidence-level or observation-based) rescue trust and team performance for an unreliable robot: with explanations a low-ability robot achieved mission success and trust comparable to a high-ability robot; explanations did nothing for the already-reliable robot.
findings.source_title: Trust Calibration within a Human-Robot Team: Comparing Automatically Generated Explanations (HRI 2016)
findings.numbers: 160 recruited/140 analysed, 2x3 design; explanation main effect on trust 6.17/6.29 vs 5.37 (none), transparency 5.96/5.52 vs 4.75; low-ability robot mission success 97.1/93.7 vs 52.2, correct decisions 91.9/87.0 vs 71.9, trust 6.15/6.07 vs 4.31 (all p<.05); high-ability robot trust 6.18/6.57/6.39 n.s.; trust-transparency r=.712
findings.relevance: Parcel's nav SR is 0.20, i.e. an unreliable robot; this is the regime where narrated confidence/observation explanations produce the largest gains.

findings.claim: A three-level hierarchical text summary of robot experience (sensory scene graph + audio -> change-triggered event lines '[t] Action / Visual observation / Auditory observation' -> subgoal summary) lets GPT-4 explain failures accurately, and the explanation nearly doubles correction-planning success.
findings.source_title: REFLECT: Summarizing Robot Experiences for Failure Explanation and Correction (CoRL 2023)
findings.numbers: RoboFail: 100 sim failures/10 AI2THOR tasks + 30 real failures/11 tasks (UR5e); explanation accuracy 88.4%, localization 96.0%, correction success 79.1% vs 41.9% without explanation; w/o audio 50.0%/68.8%; w/o progressive 46.5%/62.8%/60.5%; GPT-4
findings.relevance: Defines the representation format Model A should emit for Model B: hierarchical, time-stamped, change-triggered text, with success/failure determined by subgoal checks rather than LLM belief.

findings.claim: Real-time multimodal LLM backends (OpenAI Realtime, Gemini Live) driving a social robot give ~0.7 s turn latency but under-invoke perception tools (recall ~0.6), so robot state must be pushed into the model rather than pulled by tool calls.
findings.source_title: A Modern System Recipe for Situated Embodied Human-Robot Conversation with Real-Time Multimodal LLMs and Tool-Calling
findings.numbers: OpenAI Realtime 689.98 +/- 389.08 ms; Gemini Live 739.10 +/- 593.45 ms; tool-decision macro accuracy 0.72/0.77, precision 0.88/0.84, recall 0.62/0.60; look_at_person precision 0.52-0.68; YOLO11-pose 49.3 ms (20.37 Hz), SAM3 161.7 ms (6.18 Hz); fluency 4.62/4.42 of 5; cost $0.047 vs $0.018 per interaction; kappa 0.41; Jibo + Reachy Mini
findings.relevance: Quantifies the latency and pull-failure budget of Parcel's hosted Realtime lane; justifies the whisperer/push design and pre-computing narration lines before the hosted model speaks.

findings.claim: A streaming video-language model can learn 'when to speak' as a per-frame silent/speak decision and stay coherent over long tasks by writing an iterative progress summary into its own system prompt; large-scale synthetic dialogue data makes this trainable.
findings.source_title: Proactive Assistant Dialogue Generation from Streaming Egocentric Videos (EMNLP 2025)
findings.numbers: 30,135 dialogues / 478.7 h video from 6 egocentric datasets, synthesized with LLaMA-3.1-70B; model LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct + SigLIP-SO400M, 1/5/10 tokens per frame; negative-frame subsampling rho=0.1; LLM-judge vs human Pearson 0.67 (F1) / 0.47 (overall); 100-dialogue human eval, 81% inter-rater agreement; best-domain helpfulness 2.67/5
findings.relevance: The trainable analogue of Model B's speak/hold gate and of the 'last 1 minute / global history' summary object; its temporally aligned P/R/F1 is a ready-made timing metric.

findings.claim: Overt robot self-talk (rule-based ACT-R inner speech on Pepper, distinguished by voice tone/volume and LED colour) raised users' trust and anthropomorphism ratings after a cooperative table-setting task; the readable preprint had no control group.
findings.source_title: Robot's Inner Speech Effects on Trust and Anthropomorphic Cues in Human-Robot Cooperation
findings.numbers: N=27, post-test 15 days after pre-test; Trust Perception Scale-HRI 65.70 -> 68.91 (t(26)=-2.06, p<.05); Godspeed anthropomorphism 2.70 -> 3.31 (t=-4.20, p<.001), animacy 3.19 -> 3.78 (p<.001), perceived intelligence 3.90 -> 4.19 (p<.05), likeability 4.10 -> 4.30, safety 4.07 -> 4.04 n.s.; self-talk covariate n.s.
findings.relevance: Only direct evidence that an audible 'inner voice' changes trust; gives a concrete inner/outer utterance grammar and the voice-signature trick for distinguishing thinking from commitment.

findings.claim: Explanations that state the current action plus the last successful action plus environmental context (CB-H) best help non-experts identify a robot failure and its fix, and an encoder-decoder trained on simulation generates such explanations that perform on par with hand-scripted ones in an unseen environment.
findings.source_title: Explainable AI for Robot Failures: Generating Explanations that Improve User Assistance in Fault Recovery (HRI 2021)
findings.numbers: Study 1: 80 recruited/70 analysed; context effect on failure identification F(2,67)=6.95, p=.0018 (CB vs None t=3.729, p=.0012); history F(2,67)=3.36, p=.04; Study 2: 45/41 participants; model explanation accuracy 81.81% on 6 failure causes; generated vs None t(38)=-4.158, p=.00049; generated vs scripted t=-0.208, p=.97; GRU encoder-decoder, 60 kitchen sims / 2100 timesteps
findings.relevance: Specifies the minimum content of a narrated failure/blocked message for the owner (action + last action + context) and shows it can be learned from simulation.

findings.claim: A live narration system (RONAR) aligns robot streams at 0.2 Hz, compresses ~1,000 frames to ~30 keyframes, verbalizes environment/internal/plan state as text, and offers Alert/Info/Debug narration modes; it beats REFLECT on failure explanation but the two-stage LLM pipeline is too slow for real-time use on the robot.
findings.source_title: I Can Tell What I am Doing: Toward Real-World Natural Language Grounding of Robot Experiences (RONAR)
findings.numbers: 0.2 Hz alignment; cumulative-sum threshold 80 -> ~30 keyframes from ~1,018 frames; RoboNar: 70 demos, 4 tasks, Stretch SE3, 76 failures (54 manipulation/12 navigation/7 detection); GPT-4o; +11% failure explanation over REFLECT; narration Likert 4.50 vs 4.13, informativeness 4.56 vs 4.06, coherence 4.56 vs 4.25; CC BY 4.0
findings.relevance: Gives concrete update-rate, keyframe and mode choices for Parcel's digest, and warns that LLM-in-the-loop summarization cannot sit on the 10 Hz control path.

findings.claim: Proactive conversational AI can be built as a covert parallel thought stream gated by an intrinsic-motivation score; users preferred a moderately proactive setting over non-stop chatter or a highly selective one.
findings.source_title: Proactive Conversational Agents with Inner Thoughts (CHI 2025)
findings.numbers: Formative study N=24 (394 quotes, 8 heuristics: relevance 77 mentions, information gap 33, balance 33, coherence 30, dynamics 30, expected impact 23, originality 16, urgency 14); pause trigger 10 s; thoughts <15 words; motivation rated 1-5; memory decay lambda=0.95, saliency threshold 0.3; evaluation N=12, settings system1Prob 0.7/0.2/0, thresholds 3.59/4.09; Active Contributor preferred by 6/12; social presence median 6 vs 5.5 (p<.05)
findings.relevance: Design of Model B's speak/hold decision and its thresholds; the heuristics double as reward features for a trainable gate.

findings.claim: Training a VLA to emit an embodied chain of thought (TASK, PLAN, SUBTASK, MOVE, GRIPPER POSITION, VISIBLE OBJECTS) before each action raises success substantially, makes failures interpretable and correctable by a one-line language correction, at a ~50x token cost that async decoding partly hides.
findings.source_title: Robotic Control via Embodied Chain-of-Thought Reasoning (CoRL 2024)
findings.numbers: OpenVLA-7B base; ~2.5M Bridge-v2 transitions annotated (7 days); in-dist success 44% +/- 3.9 -> 66% +/- 3.8 (+28 abs), OOD 30% -> 64% (+34); tokens/step 7 -> ~350; 5-step freeze +24% speed (72%), async +40% speed (65%); single language correction 32% -> 80%
findings.relevance: Closest trainable precedent for Model A emitting a plan/intent representation alongside actions, with the sim-annotation recipe and the latency mitigation Parcel would need.

findings.claim: An LLM-narrating museum robot's users mostly trusted its narratives and could not detect fabricated answers; the robot spoke proactively after 45 s of silence and used GPT-4 function calling for navigation goals.
findings.source_title: NarraGuide: an LLM-based Narrative Mobile Robot for Remote Place Exploration (UIST 2025)
findings.numbers: TurtleBot3, ROS2 Nav2, GPT-4 intent classifier + per-location grounding; proactive prompt after 45 s silence; n=20; suggestions accepted M=2.90 (SD 2.32) vs rejected 0.9; 11/20 judged narratives accurate; 6 noted errors; 2 participants believed hallucinated answers about a rock they pointed at
findings.relevance: Evidence that hosted-LLM narration hallucinates undetectably; motivates a digest-only narration constraint and a measured hallucination-per-utterance rate.

findings.claim: Verbalizing the robot's dialogue-state graph into natural language before prompting the LLM raised perceived factuality of a Pepper tour robot's answers versus feeding semantic triples, with far more explicit uncertainty markers and fewer negations.
findings.source_title: A Graph-to-Text Approach to Knowledge-Grounded Response Generation in Human-Robot Interaction
findings.numbers: N=18; GPT-4 and LLaMA-2-chat; factuality GPT-Verbal 4.06 vs GPT-Triples 3.44 (Wilcoxon p=.03), LLaMA-Verbal 3.68; adequacy 3.88 vs 3.69; uncertainty markers 40 vs 6; negations 68 vs 112; residual errors mostly from undetected objects
findings.relevance: Says how to serialize Parcel's scene/state for the hosted model: verbalized sentences with explicit uncertainty, not raw triples/JSON.

findings.claim: Frontier LLMs used as embodied cognitive controllers are overconfident about task success (one model believed it succeeded in every trial), so success must be verified externally rather than taken from the model's belief.
findings.source_title: From Language to Action: Can LLM-Based Agents Be Used for Embodied Robot Cognition?
findings.numbers: GPT-4.1 / Claude 4 Sonnet / Qwen3-Coder-480B / DeepSeek-V3.1 on a PyBullet mobile manipulator; T1 success 100/100/80/100%; T2 44.4/100/66.2/75.5%; all but Claude overconfident; DeepSeek believes success in all trials
findings.relevance: Success/failure flags in the digest must come from Model A's detectors, never from the hosted voice model.

findings.claim: A fully autonomous social robot with a proactive, affect-aware dialogue policy earned substantially higher post-interaction trust than a reactive one, but the advantage shrank toward zero once sessions with ASR/communication breakdown were included.
findings.source_title: Trust in Autonomous Human-Robot Collaboration: Effects of Responsive Interaction Policies
findings.numbers: Misty-II; 29 sessions, 24 eligible (10 control/14 responsive); TI-HRC 39 (SD 22) vs 67 (21), p=.004; TPS-HRI 59 (17) vs 77 (18), p=.022; mixed model beta=16.28 (p=.005) / 14.17 (p=.046); collaborative language 42% vs 5% of turns; breakdown turns 25% vs 22% n.s.; full-sample beta ~7 with CI crossing 0
findings.relevance: Narration gains are conditional on speech-recognition viability; the mic array and barge-in handling are part of the narration design.

findings.claim: A GPT-4 tour robot that narrates its own plan steps from system-message state updates ('SYSTEM: Starting action: Drive to Apple' -> 'Off I go, driving towards the apple') was preferred by every participant over an identical silent robot, but users noticed response delay and hallucinated lab facts.
findings.source_title: Dobby: A Conversational Service Robot Driven by GPT-4
findings.numbers: gpt-4-0613 function calling (ExecutePlan/CancelPlan/ContinuePlan); 6 s silence re-prompt; 22 participants; enjoyment 6.59 vs 4.00 (7-pt); landmarks visited 5.27 vs 3.00
findings.relevance: Shows the push-state-as-system-message pattern that Parcel's whisperer already uses, plus the narrated acknowledgement idiom for accepted injections.

findings.claim: An autonomous LLM museum guide rebuilds a compact dynamic prompt at every area transition (identity, visited/unvisited areas, nearby artworks with relative position, chat history) explicitly to bound tokens and latency, and triggers proximity-based commentary; field results show many out-of-scope questions and noise-driven comprehension failures.
findings.source_title: Next-Gen Museum Guides: Autonomous Navigation and Visitor Interaction with an Agentic Robot
findings.numbers: Alter-Ego robot; GPT-4o mini with go_to()/end_tour(); 120 s no-response ends tour; N=34; mean interaction 19.2 min; 7.29 questions/visitor, 3.71 answered correctly, 2.25 out of scope, 1.26 comprehension failures; comprehension-failure rate 33.33% (noisy areas) vs 5.88% (quiet); perceived competence dropped pre->post (p=.019)
findings.relevance: Concrete prompt-rebuild-on-event pattern and realistic error rates for a narrating navigation robot.

findings.claim: Co-speech deictic actions (head turn, laser pointing, gaze) synchronized per narrated sentence by an LLM-parsed action queue made a tour-guide robot markedly more engaging and guided visual attention faster than audio-only narration.
findings.source_title: CLIO: A Tour Guide Robot with Co-speech Actions for Visual Attention Guidance and Enhanced User Engagement
findings.numbers: OpenAI o3-pro script parsing; ROS2 action servers; N=28 (mean age 25.3), within-subjects; all impression/engagement subscales p<.001; time-to-first-fixation reduced ~4-7 s on ambiguous exhibits
findings.relevance: Narration events should be tied to Go2 gestures via the gesture tool; speech alone underdelivers.

findings.claim: Humans cannot read AI reasoning text as a faithful account of what drove the output: accuracy at identifying causally influential steps was barely above chance, so reasoning traces must not be narrated as if they were the robot's actual reasons.
findings.source_title: Humans Perceive Wrong Narratives from AI Reasoning Texts
findings.numbers: 29% accuracy vs 25% chance; 42% on majority-vote high-agreement items
findings.relevance: Model B should narrate verified digest fields (blocked_by, deviation_reason), not chain-of-thought.

findings.claim: Spoken language models can interleave unspoken reasoning chunks with spoken chunks so that thinking happens during audio playback at no added latency, and a separate incremental verbalizer can turn reasoning into speech-ready text.
findings.source_title: STITCH: Simultaneous Thinking and Talking with Chunked Reasoning for Spoken Language Models (ICLR 2026); see also Think, Verbalize, then Speak (EMNLP 2025, https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.16028)
findings.numbers: +15% on math reasoning vs no-reasoning baseline; latency equal to baseline; parity on non-reasoning sets
findings.relevance: Thought-to-speech mechanism for a tightly coupled speech/motion loop: reason covertly on the digest, speak short verbalized lines.

findings.claim: The design of a transparency utterance changes how competent, benevolent and transparent users judge a robot and how many extra capabilities they infer, i.e., narration can create over-trust in capabilities the robot lacks.
findings.source_title: Towards a Systematic Model of the Effects of Transparency Utterances on Calibrating Trust in Social Robots (HRI 2026)
findings.numbers: N=47, in-person, between-subject; effect on inferred capabilities and (over-)trust confirmed; utterance texts not in readable abstract
findings.relevance: The lever for Parcel's 2/10 capability-grounding score: narration must be capability-honest by construction.

findings.claim: Navigation narration can be parameterized in a verbalization space of abstraction (raw distances/turns up to landmark/room names), locality and specificity, with detailed narratives running 55-104 words versus short general-picture summaries; different users want different points in the space.
findings.source_title: Verbalization: Narration of Autonomous Robot Experience (IJCAI 2016)
findings.numbers: 4 abstraction levels; templates such as '[I] [went through/took] the [corridor/bridge]'; detailed narratives 55-104 words; CoBot multi-floor routes
findings.relevance: Gives Model B an abstraction-selection knob so spoken progress uses landmark language and stays far shorter than detailed narratives.

findings.claim: A life-long episodic memory can be verbalized through a collapsed hierarchical tree (raw -> scene graphs -> events -> goals -> recursive summaries) that an LLM agent expands on demand, keeping per-query tokens roughly constant over months of experience.
findings.source_title: Episodic Memory Verbalization using Hierarchical Representations of Life-Long Robot Experience (H-EMV)
findings.numbers: Gemini 1.5 Pro / GPT-4o agents; TEACh up to 100 episodes (~2 months), 500 QA; Ego4D 6:43 h + 4:28 h, 40 QA; ARMAR-7 3.3 h over 2 months, 30 QA; 34% correct + 62% partially correct; ~10K tokens/query vs 1,256K flat
findings.relevance: Format for the 'global history' part of Model A's input and for answering owner questions about the past without flooding the hosted model.

findings.claim: Explainable-robotics research is dominated by question-driven, text-based, descriptive explanations about navigation, with half generated in real time and only half of papers proposing any evaluation.
findings.source_title: Generating Explanations for Autonomous Robots: a Systematic Review
findings.numbers: 22 papers (2015-2024) from 803 hits; 50% real-time; 16/22 question-driven; navigation mentioned in 15; 11/22 propose evaluation; 13 social robotics
findings.relevance: Confirms there is no established metric for proactive navigation narration; Parcel's evaluation would be filling a gap.

design_implications: Model A's narration-facing output should be a hierarchical, time-stamped, change-triggered text/JSON digest (goal/plan level; event level emitted on scene-graph, plan-state, blocked/following/battery changes; sensory level kept on-robot), mirroring REFLECT/RONAR/H-EMV; update it at roughly 0.2-1 Hz plus event triggers, not at the 10 Hz act-token rate.

Extend the StateDigest with deviation_reason, last_completed_action, environmental context, and a confidence/observation-basis field: Kox (eta^2=.177, delta 1.2 after an explained deviation) and Wang (mission success 52->97 for an unreliable robot) show these are the fields that move trust, and Das & Chernova show context+history is what lets an owner help.

Success/failure and 'done' claims must originate from Model A's detectors (subgoal checks, blocked flags), never from the hosted model's belief; three of four frontier LLMs overestimate their own success and NarraGuide/Dobby users could not detect hallucinated narration.

Model B should own a speak/hold gate: covert candidate thoughts (<15 words) scored on relevance/information-gap/urgency/balance with thresholds (Inner Thoughts), trainable as a per-frame speak/silent head with negative subsampling (ProAssist rho=0.1), plus an iterative progress summary that doubles as the 'last minute / global history' object.

Narrate short, speech-ready lines at landmark abstraction ('heading to the sofa', 'going around the chair') and keep reasoning unspoken (Think-Verbalize-Speak, STITCH); never voice chain-of-thought as the robot's reasons (humans read reasoning text at 29% accuracy).

Push state to the hosted voice model as verbalized sentences with explicit uncertainty markers (graph-to-text: factuality 4.06 vs 3.44) via the whisperer; do not rely on the hosted model pulling perception through tools (recall ~0.6 on OpenAI Realtime/Gemini Live) and pre-compute the narration line before the ~0.7 s hosted turn.

Every accepted voice injection (submit/suspend/resume/amend) should produce an event-level digest entry that Model B turns into a narrated acknowledgement ('Sure, I'll check the sofa'), following Dobby's system-message -> spoken-line pattern; tie narration events to Go2 gestures via the gesture tool (CLIO: p<.001 engagement gains from co-speech action).

Generate ECoT-style annotations (plan, subtask, blocked reason, visible objects) from the simulator's ground truth to train Model A to emit the digest; budget for the token cost (7->~350 tokens/step) with asynchronous decoding as ECoT did (+40% speed).

Make narration capability-honest by construction (Fischer & Jelinek: utterance design changes inferred capabilities, over-trust) to address the 2/10 capability-grounding score; optionally give 'inner voice' lines a distinct voice/LED signature so the owner can separate thinking from commitment (Pipitone).

Evaluation battery for the sim-to-real conversational-navigation rig: per-event trust probes around blocked/replan/failure moments (Kox T1-T8), TPS-HRI pre/post, NASA-TLX, a hallucination-per-utterance audit of narration against the digest, ProAssist-style temporally aligned speak-timing F1, RONAR 5-point naturalness/informativeness/coherence (bar 4.50), and Das & Chernova failure/solution-identification accuracy for the owner; protect ASR viability (comprehension failures 33% in noisy vs 6% in quiet areas; trust advantage collapses under breakdown).
open_questions: No fetched study measures the trust or annoyance effect of spoken status updates as a function of update frequency for a companion robot during navigation; Kox used four updates per mission and Inner Thoughts found users disliked non-stop chatter, but the optimal rate for a quadruped walking with its owner is unknown (the planned frequency/annoyance search was not run: session search budget exhausted).

No paper reports a hallucination-per-utterance rate for narration generated from a state digest; NarraGuide and Dobby report undetected hallucinations only qualitatively, so Parcel would have to define and measure this itself.

Whether a trainable, fully duplex Model A can emit a representation that is faithful to its own control decisions is untested: ECoT improves success and interpretability but does not verify that the emitted reasoning is causal, and Levy et al. show humans misread reasoning text.

The controlled (experimental vs control) numbers for Pipitone/Chella's inner-speech trust study are in the paywalled IJSR 2023/2024 version and could not be read; the arXiv preprint has N=27 pre/post only.

The HRI-2026 'Show Your Work' study (mechanistic transparency on an LLM-powered Pepper, reported to increase trust growth and perceived reliability) and Halilovic's 2024 navigation-explanation satisfaction study are ACM-403; their effect sizes are unknown.

All large trust effects come from screen-based or manipulation settings (virtual military mission, AMT reconnaissance, Misty puzzle); transfer to an embodied quadruped narrating while walking is an assumption.

Latency of an on-robot Model B (digest -> speech-ready line) on the Jetson AGX Orin was not addressed by any source; RONAR says two-stage LLM summarization is too slow, and ECoT's ~350 reasoning tokens per step would need asynchronous decoding.
Quadruped-specific narration work (Go2/Spot with LLM speech during navigation) was not found before the search budget ran out; this remains unsurveyed.

results.claim: Regular spoken status updates that include the what and why of a route deviation (e.g., 'A faster alternative route has been detected, because the river had dried up. Moving to location: right turn.') keep trust high and stable when a robot deviates from plan; silent deviation is a trust violation, and the updates add no subjective workload.
results.evidence_quote: "Participants (N = 82) engaged in a virtual military mission as a Human-Robot Team using a 2 × 2 between-subjects design ... Results showed that transparency contributed to higher and more stable levels of trust, without increasing subjective workload." Table 1 lists four audio messages per mission (1a–1d training; 2a–2d experimental), incl. "2b A faster alternative route has been detected, because the river had dried up. Moving to location: right turn." Results: "(F (1, 78) = 16.72, p < .001, η2 = .177). On average, high transparency (M = 5.1, SE = 0.1) led to higher perceived trustworthiness than low transparency (M = 4.3, SE = 0.1)." ... "(F (2.48, 234) = 12.37, p < .001, η2 = .137) ... (ΔM = 1.2, p < .001). Although this gap shrinks over time, it remains significant (T7: ΔM = 1.0, p < .001; T8: ΔM = 0.8, p = .003) ... in the low transparency condition, the robot's silent deviation before T6 results in a trust violation." ... "stronger effect for Ability (ΔM = 0.8, F (1, 78) = 31.80, p < .001, η2 = .290)" ... "on any of the NASA TLX subscales. This suggests that transparency did not affect workload." Items "rated on a 7-point Likert scale".
results.correction: None needed. All numbers verified verbatim (N=82; 2x2 between-subjects; 4 TTS messages per mission; F(1,78)=16.72, p<.001, eta^2=.177, M=5.1 vs 4.3 on 7-pt scale; transparency x time eta^2=.137; delta M 1.2 at T6, 1.0 at T7, 0.8 at T8 p=.003; Ability eta^2=.290; no NASA-TLX effect). Published ACM THRI 14(2), Article 23, Dec 2024, DOI 10.1145/3702245.

results.claim: Automatically generated explanations (confidence-level or observation-based) rescue trust and team performance for an unreliable robot: with explanations a low-ability robot achieved mission success and trust comparable to a high-ability robot; explanations did nothing for the already-reliable robot.
results.evidence_quote: "We recruited 160 participants from Amazon Mechanical Turk" ... "We excluded data from 20 (out of 160) participants ... As a result, 140 participants ... are included in the analysis." Table III (main effect of explanations): Trust 6.17*/6.29†/5.37*†; Transparency 5.96*/5.52†/4.75*†. Table IV (Low Ability Robot): Trust 6.15*/6.07†/4.31*†; Mission Success 97.1*/93.7†/52.2*†; Correct Decisions 91.9*/87.0†/71.9*† ("A PAIR OF * OR † MEANS THE DIFFERENCE ... IS STATISTICALLY SIGNIFICANT (p < .05)"); High Ability Robot: Trust 6.18/6.57/6.39, Mission Success 94.7/91.7/77.4. "trust is strongly and positively correlated with transparency, r(137) = .712, p < .001". "explanations made no significant difference on any of the dependent variables, when participants worked with a high-ability robot." "participants did not succeed in significantly more missions when they worked with a high-ability robot. This may be an indication that the explanations offered by the low-ability robot were mitigating the impact of its erroneous recommendations." "The 2x3 ANOVA tests also show significant main effects of explanation on trust, F (2, 133) = 17.23, p < .0001".
results.correction: None needed. All numbers verified verbatim. Note the paper does not run a direct statistical contrast across ability levels ('it makes little sense to compare across robots of different abilities'); 'comparable' rests on the Table IV means (low-ability w/ explanation trust 6.15/6.07 and success 97.1/93.7 vs high-ability 6.18/6.57/6.39 and 94.7/91.7) plus the authors' statement that high-ability teams did not succeed in significantly more missions.

results.claim: A three-level hierarchical text summary of robot experience (sensory scene graph + audio -> change-triggered event lines '[t] Action / Visual observation / Auditory observation' -> subgoal summary) lets GPT-4 explain failures accurately, and the explanation nearly doubles correction-planning success.
results.evidence_quote: Sensory-input summary "converts multisensory robot observations (RGB-D, sound, robot states) into task-informed scene graphs and audio summary"; event-based summary format "[timestep] Action: [robot action] Visual observation: object1 [state], object2... Auditory observation: [audio summary]."; "a frame is selected if it satisfies any of the conditions below: 1) The task-informed scene graph of the current frame G_t is different from the previous frame G_{t-1}. 2) The frame is the start or end of an audio event. 3) The frame marks the end of a subgoal execution." "We use GPT-4 as the LLM". RoboFail: "100 failure scenarios, with 10 cases for each of the 10 tasks" (AI2THOR) and "30 failure scenarios" across "11 tasks" with a "UR5e robot arm". Table 1 (sim, execution failure Exp/Loc/Co-plan): REFLECT 88.4/96.0/79.1; w/o progressive 46.5/62.8/60.5; w/o explanation —/—/41.9 (planning failure: REFLECT 84.2/80.7/80.7 vs w/o explanation 56.1). Table 2 (real, execution Exp/Loc): w/o sound 50.0/68.8; REFLECT 68.8/93.8. arXiv Comments: "Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL) 2023".
results.correction: Claim and numbers hold. Two precision notes: (a) 'w/o audio 50.0%/68.8%' are the REAL-WORLD execution-failure Exp/Loc cells (row labelled 'w/o sound'), whereas 88.4/96.0/79.1 vs 41.9 and 'w/o progressive 46.5/62.8/60.5' are SIMULATION execution-failure cells; 'nearly doubles' (79.1 vs 41.9) applies to execution failures, planning failures improve 56.1 -> 80.7. (b) The relevance note 'success/failure determined by subgoal checks rather than LLM belief' is inaccurate for REFLECT: subgoal satisfaction is judged by the LLM from the subgoal-based summary ('Q: Is the subgoal satisfied? A: Yes'); only the correction-planning metric uses a programmatic final-state check ('Task success is determined by comparing the final state and the specified goal condition').

results.claim: Real-time multimodal LLM backends (OpenAI Realtime, Gemini Live) driving a social robot give ~0.7 s turn latency but under-invoke perception tools (recall ~0.6), so robot state must be pushed into the model rather than pulled by tool calls.
results.evidence_quote: "both backends exhibit similar latency on average (OpenAI Realtime: 690±389 ms; Gemini Live: 739±593 ms), with substantial variance that likely reflects natural heterogeneity in turn structure and streaming end-of-turn detection." Tool-decision macro: OpenAI Realtime Accuracy 0.72±0.10, Precision 0.88±0.18, Recall 0.62±0.23; Gemini Live 0.77±0.07 / 0.84±0.16 / 0.60±0.22; look_at_person precision 0.52 / 0.68; YOLO11-pose 49.3±3.50 ms (20.37 Hz), SAM3 161.7±4.31 ms (6.18 Hz); fluency 4.62±0.43 / 4.42±0.85; cost $0.047±0.013 / $0.018±0.002; Cohen's kappa 0.41; Jibo, with "the same recipe on a second platform (Reachy Mini)". "models learn a 'safe' policy that avoids unnecessary calls, but in embodied interaction, not looking is itself an error". Proposed fix: "future optimization should target calibration and coverage (when to look) as much as correctness (how to look), potentially via costs that penalize missed perceptual actions, state features that expose perceptual uncertainty, or training data that includes repair-heavy episodes." On use_vision: "rather than continuously streaming video to the LM, which can be costly as image tokens accumulate ... the system can request visual information ... only when it is necessary."
results.correction: All numbers and the under-invocation finding are supported (recall 0.62/0.60; latency ~0.69-0.74 s). But the conclusion 'so robot state must be pushed into the model rather than pulled by tool calls' is NOT stated by the paper: its recommended remedies are better tool calibration/coverage (penalties for missed perceptual actions, uncertainty-exposing state features, repair-heavy training data) and making tools 'return structured state'; it deliberately keeps use_vision on-demand for token cost. The push-design inference is the reviewer's own. Also note the small evaluation base: two annotators (35F, 18F) rating 24 videos (6 scenarios x 4 variants), and the latency metric's measurement boundaries are not precisely defined (Table IV 'Latency (ms)').

results.claim: A streaming video-language model can learn 'when to speak' as a per-frame silent/speak decision and stay coherent over long tasks by writing an iterative progress summary into its own system prompt; large-scale synthetic dialogue data makes this trainable.
results.evidence_quote: "30,135 dialogues across 479 hours of video" (Table 1 total: 478.7) from six egocentric datasets (Ego4D, EpicKitchen, HoloAssist, Assembly101, EgoExoLearn, WTaG), synthesized with "LLaMA-3.1-70B-Instruct"; model "LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct" + "SigLIP-SO400M", I=1/5/10 tokens per frame; "ρ=0.1". "Learning when to speak can be framed as a sequence of binary decisions, where at each step the model must choose between speaking and remaining silent"; "At each frame, it predicts whether to respond...generating [EOS] to remain silent". "Generation then resumes with this summary incorporated into the initial system prompt for the next processing segment". Human eval: "We uniformly sampled 100 dialogues from the test split", "inter-rater agreement of 81%". Table 3 (Pearson / Spearman): F1 vs Human 0.35* / 0.32*; Overall vs Human 0.47** / 0.44**; Overall vs F1 0.67** / 0.64**. Table 8 best domain: WTaG 2.67. Semantic Scholar venue: "Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing", 2025 (arXiv page carries no comments/venue).
results.correction: The claim text itself is supported (per-frame speak/silent decision; iterative progress summary written into the system prompt; 30,135 synthetic dialogues / 478.7 h / 6 datasets / LLaMA-3.1-70B; LLaMA-3.1-8B + SigLIP-SO400M, 1/5/10 tokens per frame; rho=0.1; 100-dialogue human eval, 81% agreement; best-domain helpfulness 2.67/5 on WTaG). The correlation numbers are mislabelled: corrected statement — 'LLM-judge overall score vs human: Pearson 0.47 (Spearman 0.44); automatic temporally-aligned F1 vs human: Pearson 0.35 (Spearman 0.32); LLM-judge overall vs F1 metric: Pearson 0.67 (Spearman 0.64).' The 0.67 is judge-vs-F1, not judge-vs-human. EMNLP 2025 is confirmed only via Semantic Scholar; the arXiv v1 page/API lists no venue.

sweeps.topic: Sim-to-real for language-driven navigation on Unitree Go2/Go1 and human-in-the-loop LLM demos (NaVILA, LOVON, TIC-VLA, NavDP, HA-VLN 2.0, Isaac Lab/Sim + Go2, Habitat 3.0 HITL, PARTNR, TartanGround, tau-Voice, Go2 ROS2 + LLM voice community stacks)

findings.claim: NaVILA (8B VLM + Isaac-Lab locomotion policy) runs its language loop off-robot at ~1 s per action and reached 88% real-world success on 25 Go2 instructions; on-robot deployment of the VLM is explicitly left as future work.
findings.source_title: NaVILA: Legged Robot Vision-Language-Action Model for Navigation
findings.numbers: VLA inference ~0.6 s/sample; ~1 s wait between actions; 8-frame memory; actions {forward, left, right, stop} -> {0.5 m/s, +/-pi/6 rad/s, 0}; VLN-CE-Isaac 1,077 of 1,839 R2R val-unseen trajectories; Go2 vision SR 50.2 (NE 5.49) vs blind 36.2; H1 45.3 vs 24.4; real: 25 instructions x3 repeats, 88% SR, 75% on complex; locomotion PPO 60K FPS on RTX 4090; LiDAR 15 Hz, 360x90 deg height map; 2K YouTube videos -> 20K trajectories; quantisation halves memory, +40% speed; code Apache-2.0 (705 stars), VLN-CE-Isaac MIT (Isaac Sim 4.1 / Lab 1.1, VLM server >=24 GB VRAM)
findings.relevance: Direct template for Parcel's slow-language/fast-locomotion split and discrete act-token vocabulary; shows an 8B model is off-board on a Go2.

findings.claim: TIC-VLA decouples a 10 Hz action policy from 0.5 Hz VLM reasoning, trains with random 0-10 s reasoning delays, and loses ~10 SR points on a real Go2 when moved from a laptop GPU to a Jetson Orin NX purely from latency.
findings.source_title: TIC-VLA: A Think-in-Control Vision-Language-Action Model for Robot Navigation in Dynamic Environments
findings.numbers: InternVL3-1B (InternViT-300M + Qwen2.5-0.5B); policy 10 Hz, reasoning 0.5 Hz; latency policy/reasoning 85.73/3430.73 ms on RTX 4060 (50 W), 120.27/4831.73 ms on Orin NX (25 W); reasoning delay U[0,10] s in training; DynaNav (Isaac Sim) 85 test cases, up to 200 pedestrians; sim SR 55.29, NE 10.55, CR 28.24; real Go2 SR 0.85 (RTX 4060) vs 0.75 (Orin NX); data 8.7 h SCAND + 11 h GND + 5.1 h sim
findings.relevance: Closest published analogue to Model A's duplex frame clock; gives the on-Orin latency budget and the recipe of training under injected slow-loop delay.

findings.claim: NavDP trains a navigation diffusion policy entirely in Isaac Sim at 2,500 trajectories/GPU/day and transfers zero-shot to a Go2 at 7/10 real-world point-goal success; adding real-to-sim Gaussian-splat data raises success by 30%.
findings.source_title: NavDP: Learning Sim-to-Real Navigation Diffusion Policy with Privileged Information Guidance
findings.numbers: 200K+ trajectories, >1M m, 3,154 scenes, 452 h, 40M images; 2,500 traj/GPU/day (20x real-world efficiency); 32 A100 training; inference >>10 Hz; real: TurtleBot4 9/10, Go2 7/10, G1 7/10, avg 76.7% vs ViPlanner 53.3%; sim Dingo 67.2% SR / 62.6% SPL; real-to-sim data +30% SR; repo CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (773 stars), benchmark IsaacSim 4.2 / IsaacLab 1.2
findings.relevance: Quantifies embodiment gap (wheeled vs Go2) and sim data throughput; non-commercial licence blocks product training.

findings.claim: LOVON runs an LLM planner + YOLO-11 + a tiny language-to-motion transformer on a Jetson Orin across Go2/B2/H1-2, with the motion model trained in ~1 h on 1M procedurally generated samples.
findings.source_title: LOVON: Legged Open-Vocabulary Object Navigator
findings.numbers: DeepSeek R1 planner; YOLO-11; L2MM dim 256, 4 layers, 8 heads; 1M samples (4:1 split), ~1 h on RTX 3080 Ti; 1M samples generated in <15 min on i9-12900KF; Gym-Unreal max 500 steps, 500/1.00; 1.5 h training vs TrackVLA 360 h; speeds 0.3/0.5/0.7 m/s; Jetson Orin + D435i; repo MIT (108 stars) with Go2 deployment code
findings.relevance: Shows Model B's command->plan head can be trained from templated synthetic data and run on-Orin.

findings.claim: HA-VLN 2.0 validated a sim-trained human-aware VLN policy on a Go2-EDU (Jetson NX + RPi 4B) and measured that 2-4 free-moving people cut real-world navigation success from 0.44 to 0.18; human-aware sim training gave 0.18 vs 0.12 for plain VLN-CE training.
findings.source_title: HA-VLN 2.0: An Open Benchmark and Leaderboard for Human-Aware Navigation in Discrete and Continuous Environments with Dynamic Multi-Human Interactions
findings.numbers: 16,844 instructions (10,819/778/1,839/3,408); HAPS 2.0 486 motion sequences, 910 human models, 90 scans, 430 annotation h; sim up to 10 humans at 30-60 FPS on one 24 GB GPU; sim baseline SR 0.05, NE 7.82; real Go2-EDU with D435i + MID360 + IMU, Jetson NX inference, RPi 4B motion, 0.25 m steps, 15 deg turns, panoramic rotate per step; 4 region types x 3 instances x 30 trials; NSR ALL: HA-VLN-VL(HA-VLN) 0.44 w/o humans / 0.18 w/ humans; HA-VLN-VL(VLN-CE) 0.40 / 0.12; CMA-Base 0.25/0.15 and 0.26/0.09; repo MIT (401 stars), Go2 code not included
